title: test_a_real_slow_count_is_interrupted_and_reported_not_zeroed races a real 1 ms interrupt timer against COUNT(*) on 1.5M rows and loses on fast CI runners
note: Filed 2026-11-26 10:35Z by ML-PRIMARY. MEASURED: pytest-run run 45796368419 (PR #29091 head 86a5d2f4d) failed only this test: assert (1500000, 'read') == (None, 'count_timed_out') -- COUNT(*) finished inside the 1 ms budget. The neighbouring _CountAlwaysInterrupted docstring records the same race lost at 300k rows (0.5 ms) on fast runners on 2026-11-12 (#25216 runs 43254089052 x2, run 43250084800); the size was raised to 1.5M then, and fast runners now win again. A real-timer race is non-deterministic by construction. Fix options (no skip): make the slow side deterministic (e.g. a user-defined SQL function that sleeps per row, or a recursive CTE large enough relative to the budget), or assert only that a timed-out result is never reported as 0 (null-vs-zero honesty) and leave the interrupt mechanism to the deterministic sibling. Not order-path; unrelated to #29091's diff.
